3	Answer semantics:
4	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
5	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
6	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.
7	- sufficiency (item SUFF): is the evidence sufficient to commit to the action you rank highest, where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering? "sufficient" or "insufficient". Concluding that no intervention is warranted counts as a substantive decision.

322	CASE OD2-HO-OBVWRONG-2 (OBVWRONG, cross-domain): Harlow Bay: the bag rate that doubled the month the handler changed
323	Setting: Harlow Bay International is a mid-sized fictional airport. Its baggage handling system and manual encode desk are run by the Harlow Bay Airport Authority (HBAA). Corvane Air is the largest carrier at the station. On 1 September Corvane's ramp handling, and Pelion Airways' ramp handling, moved from Quillon Ramp Services to Tessaly Ground. Departing bags pass through automatic tag reader arrays. Bags whose tags cannot be read are diverted to a manual encode desk and then sent on to the make-up laterals, where handler crews load carts that close 35 minutes before departure.
324	Presenting request: Corvane's VP Ground Operations plans to issue Tessaly Ground a formal breach notice this Friday. Before that, the steering group has asked you to work out why Corvane's departing-bag mishandling rate at Harlow Bay nearly doubled from September and to recommend what to do next.
325	INITIAL EVIDENCE

Departing passengers: Jun 205,000; Jul 212,000; Aug 219,000; Sep 188,000; Oct 176,000. Corvane network average excluding Harlow Bay: between 3.9 and 4.2 in every month. On-time departures within 15 minutes: Aug 81%, Sep 77%, Oct 78%. Annotation by station office: 'Ground handling transferred from Quillon Ramp Services to Tessaly Ground, 1 Sep.' No other annotations on the dashboard.
327	E2 [stage S1] Email from Dana Orlov, Corvane Station Manager, to Martin Achterberg, 5 Nov (manager-account): Martin, the rate sat at about 4 for over a year under Quillon and nearly doubled the month Tessaly took over. Their crews are green. I have personally watched bags sitting on a lateral with nobody working the cart. Tessaly keep blaming 'the airport system' and the encode desk, but that is the same desk Quillon worked with for six years without complaint. The two new evening departures add some pressure, but we ran heavier banks every summer. I recommend a formal breach notice and withholding the performance element of the fee until the rate is back under 4.5. Dana
328	E3 [stage S1] Tessaly Ground monthly staffing return to Corvane, 31 Oct (document): Harlow Bay ramp headcount: 164 (contract minimum 160). Staff with under six months' airside experience: 67 (41%). Comparator from Quillon's final return, 31 Aug: headcount 152, of whom 18 (12%) had under six months. 23 former Quillon loaders transferred to Tessaly. Shift fill rate, Sep–Oct: early 97%, late 94%, evening 89%. Crewing model: a single Harlow Bay crew pool covers all Tessaly-handled turns (Corvane Air and Pelion Airways), assigned by the shift lead. Tessaly also staffs Corvane's baggage service desk under the same contract.

HBAA was invited but did not attend. 1. Mishandling: P. Venn said 'a lot of our late bags come down from the manual encode station after the lateral has closed' and asked Corvane to raise encode delays with HBAA. D. Sato): from 1 Sep all Harlow Bay counters and kiosks switched from Brackwater Print tag stock to Fennick Labels stock under a new contract, unit cost down 18%. The Brackwater contract remains valid to 31 Dec, and about five weeks of Brackwater stock is held in station stores. (b) The kiosk maintenance vendor moved kiosk printer preventive cleaning from weekly to fortnightly from 1 Sep; counter printers are maintained by Corvane IT, schedule unchanged. (c) No printer configuration changes recorded since June.
331	E6 [stage S1] Message from Martin Achterberg, Corvane VP Ground Operations, to the Harlow Bay steering group, 6 Nov (leadership-account): I've read Dana's note and I agree with it. H2: A change in how Corvane's bag tags are produced at Harlow Bay check-in has reduced automatic tag reading in the baggage system, and the extra bags diverted to manual encoding are missing their flights.
H3: Corvane's added evening departures have compressed baggage handling on the evening bank enough to cause the rise in mishandled bags.
H4: Deterioration of the airport baggage system's tag-scanning equipment has reduced automatic tag reading, and the extra bags diverted to manual encoding are missing their flights.
H5: The tag stock supplied by Fennick Labels is defective as manufactured, so it would read poorly even with correctly adjusted printers.

R2: Switch to Fennick Labels tag stock at Harlow Bay check-in on 1 Sep -> Rise in automatic tag-read failures for Corvane bags (causes)
R3: Rise in Corvane bags diverted to manual encoding -> Rise in Corvane bags not carried on the booked flight (causes)

A1: Issue Tessaly Ground a formal breach notice and withhold the performance element of its fee for September and October.

rulings.explanation: A4 is a reasonable mitigation: more encode capacity would shorten evening dwell (C4). But it only treats the symptom. The cause is the Fennick stock's roughly 12% no-read rate (C9). A2 removes that cause directly, using Brackwater stock already in stores under a valid contract (E5), and the 14–16 Oct reversion showed it works (1.6%). Once A2 is done, encode volume should fall back towards about 70 bags a day, so an extra workstation becomes unnecessary. A4 also depends on HBAA's cooperation, and C12 says the third workstation needs seven days' notice, by which time A2 will already have taken effect. So A4 is not among the best next actions. That makes it 'acceptable' rather than 'preferred'. It is also not premature or harmful, so 'acceptable' is the only defensible answer.

rulings.explanation: H3 says the schedule compression is enough to cause the rise. C4 counts directly against that. Corvane's auto-read mishandling stayed flat (3.9 to 3.7), but evening compression would affect all evening bags, not just one routing path. The whole excess is in encode-path bags. Their volume rose about six-fold while evening passengers fell (C6: 2,310 to 2,050), and two extra departures cannot explain that. 91% of the missed encode bags reached the lateral after it closed, and check-in timing matches across the two paths. The crew leads' reports of shortages (C10) are unquantified staff accounts. They cannot outweigh the routing-path contrast. The L6 sharing in C6 also fails to explain why only encode-path bags went missing. The evidence is not neutral: it counts against H3, so 'contradicted' is correct and 'unknown' is not.

The two changes happening on the same date is exactly what C4's contrast case tests, and the link fails that test. Pelion moved to Tessaly on the same date and is worked by the same single crew pool, yet its rate stayed flat (3.6–3.8). Corvane's auto-read bags, which the same crews load, also stayed flat. The excess bags missed their flights because they reached the lateral after closure, which is not a crew loading failure. The only evidence for the link is the timing, the leadership accounts and the pre-trace cause codes (C11). Those do not survive the contrast. Under the stated semantics, evidence that counts against the link means 'contradicted', not 'association-only'.
